SUPPLEMENTAL DIRECT TESTIMONY OF
BRUCE L, JAMES
I.     INTRODUCTION
Q.	ARE YOU THE SAME BRUCE L. JAMES THAT GAVE PREVIOUS DIRECT TESTIMONY FILED ON MAY 10, 2026, AND SUPPLEMENTAL TESTIONY OF MAY 11, 2026?
A.	Yes, I am.
Q.	AFTER READING OTHER INTERVENORS DIRECT AND REBUTTAL TESTIMONY, ARE THERE OTHER CONCERNS YOU WHAT LIKE TO CALL TO THE ALJ’S AND PUC’S ATTENTION?
A.	Yes, there are.
II.     TRANSMISSION TOWER LIGHTING
Q.	WHAT IN YOUR BACKGROUND HAS RAISED THOSE CONCERNS?
A.	I hold a Commercial Pilot Certificate with multi-engine and instrument ratings as well as a Lear Jet type rating.  I have over 5,900 hours of flight time logged as a pilot.  I have flown in and out of Curtis Field in Brady, Texas many times in my flying career.  I have also flown over the Reata Ranch in both fixed wing and rotor aircraft on many occasions.  We have participated with the United States Army in the use of our ranch along with the Quinn Ranch (our cousins) in actual maneuvers on both sides of the San Saba River that included the use of transport and attack type helicopters.  Military helicopters fly over our ranch on a regular basis, and we welcome them doing so.  My dad, uncles, father-in law, all being veterans of WWII, and now gone, would expect nothing less from our family in patriotic support of our country. 

Q.	WHAT SPECIFIC CONCERNS HAS YOUR BACKGROUND IN FLYING NOW RAISED? 
A.	We were told at the public meeting in Menard, Texas in 2025 that the transmission towers for the Oncor/LCRA 765kV project now at issue would be around 155 feet tall to as much as 180 feet tall.  If that is true, then those heights implicate FAA AC 70/7460-1M, “Obstruction Lighting and Marking.”  As I read this Federal Aviation Administration Advisory Circular, all towers of the type proposed by Oncor/LCRA that are less than 150 feet in height must have a double steady red light marking the top of the transmission tower operating at night and all transmission towers over 150 feet but less than 350 feet must have  a flashing red light at the rate of 30 fpm (flashes per minute) operating at night. 
Q. 	HOW WOULD THESE LIGHTED TRANSMISSION TOWERS AFFECT YOUR RANCH USE AND ENJOYMENT?
A.	One of our family’s and friends’ great joys on the Reata has been watching the stars, satellite traffic, the International Space Station passing overhead at night, return of space shuttles, and the billions of stars in the sky at night. I never saw anything like this when I lived in Houston, San Antonio or Fort Worth.  One of the darkest areas on our ranch is in the Double M and 4-Way Pastures which are basically free of peripheral city and industrial lights. The dark night sky of our Texas Hill Country ranch that so many people from around Texas come to see for celestial events will be destroyed and is a treasured asset of ours.  I fear the Oncor/LCRA transmission towers will bring not only the ugliness of the structures themselves but accompanying light pollution.  Having 4 or more transmission towers proposed across our ranch alone with red lights blinking at the rate of 30 flashes per minute will destroy this once treasured aspect of our ranch   The same will be true of all our neighboring ranches that enjoy the same kind of outdoor adventures at night that we all have enjoyed.  
III.   CONCLUSION
Q.	WHAT IS YOUR REQUEST TO THE COMMISSION?
A.	We again respectfully ask the Commission to avoid approving any requested route suggested by Oncor/LCRA and particular any that includes or that uses Link M22.  I know that the ranchers of McCulloch County represent what is good about our great State of Texas.  Texas can do much better than the current routing proposed that would surely adversely impact the rural citizen’s way of life and the San Saba River corridor.  Is this really worth the destruction to our beautiful Hill Country?  
Q.	DOES THAT CONCLUDE YOUR SECOND SUPPLEMENTAL DIRECT TESTIMONY?
A.	Yes.
